subject: The workshop today (reply to Tilen) and the future workshops

messages.author: d2a04571097d2bcb
messages.subject: The workshop today (reply to Tilen) and the future workshops
parts:
Hi Tilen,

> it is a bit unclear to me... when is the next meeting?
> Is it taking place today or not?

No, as far as I know it is not. Although Luka's mail was right on target, it's not so easy to get the ball rolling.

I've been so far discussing this with Maarten, and we agreed to suggest first having an "advanced" meeting after the new year (of course, everyone would be invited) according to the monthly schedule we agreed on at the first meeting. Besides starting with the hands-on principle in the topics that would be presented, we would discuss how to organize the beginner workshops and distribute the workload of preparing the workshops. I suggest that we should prepare a draft agenda before the new year, and post it on the mailing list for a public discussion.

So, the beginner workshops would then (probably) begin in late January or early February.

The problem is that there is a lot of work to prepare a good hands-on workshop. There were enough people indicating their willingness to participate, but we do need to get organized.

What does everyone think about this?

Tomaz

Hey,

this is quite a self-explicatory results section that hardly needs a
discussion! As far as I've understood we are meeting again next week
(Thursday 17th at 16.00???) with another of the introductory sections
plus a coffee and a possible open ("advanced") discussion after the
main event (say, at 17.30?). Haha! I would be very happy to come and
get my first homework before Xmas! What do you say?

Guys, thumbs up for your effort!

Luka

messages.subject: RE: [Rkoholiki] The workshop today (reply to Tilen) and the future workshops
parts:
I totally agree, if the relaxed open discussion is suddenly turned into a course, there will for sure need to be a decent amount of planing and organisation involved. It was never my intetion to bring confusion or stress to the ‘advanced guys’, and of course I have my homework in the useful links that Roman had provided. But I am very pleased to learn that Tomaž and Maarten are seriously considering the idea of a beginner workshop (for them, this will be just extra work) and a few weeks’ wait shoudn’t be a problem for anyone; in the mean time, try

>with(Name_Surname, get.Rknowledge(level=basic, interval=EveryNowAndThen, mode=fun))

Luka
